title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Week 5: Top Additions, Stash Picks & Drops to Boost Your Lineup
body:
Fantasy football managers are finally getting a breather from the usual mid‑season panic as Week 5 brings only two NFL teams on bye—Kansas City and Carolina. The reduced roster turnover means waiver wires are less crowded, but the limited pool of available talent still offers opportunities for savvy owners to tighten lineups, stash future assets and cut underperformers before the next wave of injuries hits. Experts have scoured the latest performances, injury reports and schedule nuances to compile a concise list of players worth adding, keeping on the bench and dropping as the league moves deeper into its early stretch.

Quarterback depth remains a premium, especially after Patrick Mahomes’ early‑season slump and the Chiefs’ bye. Backup quarterback Jeff Gordon, who has been quietly efficient in limited snaps for the Detroit Lions, emerges as a low‑cost streaming option for teams facing a tough matchup in Week 5. His dual‑threat ability to pick up yards on the ground adds a floor that many traditional backups lack. Conversely, veteran Jameis Winston, who was claimed by the Steelers last week, has shown little upside against a stout Buffalo defense and should be considered for a drop to free up a roster spot for a more reliable option such as the newly active rookie quarterback Trey Lance.

Running backs present a mixed bag. The surprise breakout of rookie Jamaal Williams with the Detroit Lions has continued, as he logged a 16‑yard reception and a 45‑yard rush in Sunday’s game, pushing his fantasy value above his current ADP. Adding Williams now could pay dividends, especially for managers whose starters are facing the high‑powered defenses of the Baltimore Ravens and the New England Patriots. On the opposite end, veteran running back James Conner, still nursing a lingering ankle issue, has seen his touches dwindle and is projected to be inactive for the Panthers’ bye. Dropping Conner now will free a slot for a more reliable handcuff such as Alexander Mattison, who is expected to see an increased workload in Minnesota’s upcoming run‑heavy schedule.

Wide receivers are the most volatile position this week, with several players seeing their fantasy fortunes swing dramatically. The most compelling add is rookie wideout Jahan Dotson of the Washington Commanders, who posted a 71‑yard touchdown reception against the Vikings and has now become the primary target for quarterback Taylor Heath. Dotson’s target share is projected to climb further as the Commanders’ offense leans heavily on the passing game in the next two weeks. In contrast, veteran veteran Allen Robinson, who was a consistent starter for the Jets, saw a sharp decline after a week‑long suspension and a subsequent benching; his limited role in a run‑first offense suggests he is a candidate for release.

Tight ends often get overlooked, but the emergence of rookie tight end Dalton Kincaid with the Buffalo Bills provides a low‑risk stash for managers looking to hedge against injuries at the position. Kincaid’s 6.2 yards per reception and three red‑zone targets in his first three games indicate a growing rapport with quarterback Josh Allen. On the flip side, veteran tight end Zach Ertz, still on the Titans’ roster, has been inactive for two weeks and appears unlikely to return before the bye, making him a prudent drop for teams needing a roster spot for a more active contributor.

Defensive units and special teams are less fluid this week, but the Buffalo Bills’ defense has been a consistent source of points, especially in the turnover column. Managers who have yet to claim a top‑tier defense should consider the Bills as a reliable weekly starter, while the underperforming New York Giants defense, plagued by blown coverages and a lackluster pass rush, is a clear candidate for a drop.

Looking ahead, the waiver landscape will tighten further as the league approaches the full slate of bye weeks in Weeks 6 and 7. Owners who act decisively now—adding high‑upside players like Jeff Gordon, Jamaal Williams and Jahan Dotson while shedding laggards such as James Conner and Allen Robinson—will position themselves to navigate the upcoming roster churn with minimal disruption. The key will be to monitor injury updates closely, anticipate schedule matchups, and keep an eye on emerging talent that can provide both immediate production and long‑term value as the fantasy season intensifies.
